If you seeLook at
COUNT MISMATCH by a few movesa special rule in stage_targets: castling squares, double pushes, en passant
right count, MOVE MISMATCHan order problem: promotion order or stage order
move_gen hunga state that never leaves: open the waveform on state
missing moves when few pieces are leftmovers for one type: check the pawn color

30The search core: frame, stack and services

Goal: set up everything the alpha-beta state machine needs: its registers, the two RAMs, the generator, the evaluator, and one attack tester.

Concept

Step 21 showed the plan: the current node in registers, the ancestors in the stack RAM. The frame holds every variable from the C negamax that must survive a recursive call:

In CFrame fieldBits
alpha, beta, bestalpha, beta, best16 each
depthdepth5
loop index iindex8
ncount8
any_legalany_legal1
checkin_check1

The position (780 bits) plus this frame (71 bits) is one stack row: 851 bits, pushed or popped through one RAM port in one clock. The root's best move is not in the frame, since only the root needs it; one register, root_move, remembers which root move is being searched.

One more saving: the design has one attack tester, a full side_attacks circuit, which is large. Its input is always the child register, and it answers two different questions:

  • in S_TEST: did the move just made leave the mover's king (or castling path) attacked?
  • in S_ENTER: is the side to move in check? At that moment child holds the same position as pos, because entering a child copies it into pos and child already held it.
Code

The ports. The search is started with a pulse on start, and reports with a pulse on done. perft_mode turns the same machine into a perft counter, which tests almost every part of the core.

Create rtl/search_core.svpart 1 of 8
// search_core.sv - the alpha-beta recursion written as a state machine.
// "pos" and "f" hold the current node; the stack RAM holds all its ancestors.
`timescale 1ns / 1ps
module search_core
  import chess_pkg::*;
(
    input  logic               clk,
    input  logic               rst,
    input  logic               start,       // one-clock pulse while busy = 0
    input  logic               abort,       // takes effect at the next node
    input  position_t          root,
    input  logic [4:0]         depth,
    input  logic               perft_mode,  // count leaves instead of searching
    input  logic [31:0]        node_limit,  // 0 = no limit
    output logic               busy,
    output logic               done,        // one-clock pulse at the end
    output logic               aborted,
    output logic               fault,
    output move_t              best_move,   // 0 = no legal move
    output logic signed [15:0] best_score,
    output logic [47:0]        nodes,       // perft mode: leaves
    output logic [47:0]        cycles
);
  localparam logic signed [15:0] SCORE_INF  = 16'sd32000;
  localparam logic signed [15:0] SCORE_MATE = 16'sd30000;

The frame, the stack row, the sixteen states, and the registers. ret carries a score from a finished node back up to its parent: the hardware version of a function's return value.

Add to rtl/search_core.svpart 2 of 8
  // Everything the C function keeps in local variables across its recursive
  // call. The position itself is the local variable "p".
  typedef struct packed {
    logic signed [15:0] alpha;
    logic signed [15:0] beta;
    logic signed [15:0] best;
    logic [4:0]         depth;
    logic [7:0]         index;       // next move to try
    logic [7:0]         count;       // moves in this node's list
    logic               any_legal;
    logic               in_check;
  } frame_t;

  typedef struct packed {
    position_t pos;
    frame_t    f;
  } node_t;

  typedef enum logic [3:0] {
    S_IDLE, S_ENTER, S_CLASSIFY, S_EVAL_WAIT, S_GEN_START, S_GEN_WAIT,
    S_NEXT, S_READ, S_DECODE, S_APPLY, S_TEST, S_LEGAL, S_END_NODE, S_RETURN, S_POP, S_SCORE
  } state_t;

  state_t    state;
  logic [4:0] ply;
  position_t pos, child;
  frame_t    f;
  move_t     move_r, root_move;
  decoded_move_t decoded;
  logic signed [15:0] ret;           // score returned by the node that just finished
  logic      abort_pending, limit_on;
  logic      attacked;       // result of the attack test, one clock later

Line by line

  1. frame_t holds every local variable of the C negamax that must survive the recursive call: the window (alpha, beta), best, the remaining depth, the loop index, the list length, and two flags. Scores are 16-bit signed: ±32,000 fits.
  2. node_t is a frame plus its position: one row of the stack RAM, 780 + 71 = 851 bits.
  3. The state names follow the table above. Sixteen states fit in 4 bits.
  4. pos and f are the current node. child is the position after the move being tried. ret carries a finished node's score up to its parent, like a C return value.

The services: the move generator and its RAM, the stack RAM, and the evaluator. Look at the stack RAM's ports: it writes {pos, f} at row ply on a legal move, and always reads row ply − 1, the parent.

Add to rtl/search_core.svpart 3 of 8
  // ---- services ------------------------------------------------------------
  logic  gen_start, gen_done, gen_overflow, gen_we;
  logic  [7:0]  gen_count;
  logic  [12:0] gen_waddr;
  move_t gen_wdata;
  logic  stand_pat;
  assign stand_pat = (f.depth == 5'd0) && !f.in_check && !perft_mode;

  move_gen u_move_gen (
    .clk, .rst, .start(gen_start), .pos, .captures_only(stand_pat), .ply,
    .done(gen_done), .count(gen_count), .overflow(gen_overflow),
    .we(gen_we), .waddr(gen_waddr), .wdata(gen_wdata)
  );

  move_t move_rdata;
  sdp_ram #(.WIDTH($bits(move_t)), .DEPTH(8192)) u_move_ram (
    .clk, .we(gen_we), .waddr(gen_waddr), .wdata(gen_wdata),
    .raddr({ply, f.index}), .rdata(move_rdata)
  );

  logic  stack_we;
  logic  [4:0] stack_raddr;
  node_t stack_rdata;
  sdp_ram #(.WIDTH($bits(node_t)), .DEPTH(MAX_PLY)) u_stack_ram (
    .clk, .we(stack_we), .waddr(ply), .wdata({pos, f}),
    .raddr(stack_raddr), .rdata(stack_rdata)
  );
  assign stack_we    = (state == S_LEGAL) && !attacked;
  assign stack_raddr = ply - 5'd1;

  logic eval_start, eval_valid;
  logic signed [15:0] eval_score;
  eval_pipe u_eval (
    .clk, .rst, .start(eval_start), .pos, .valid(eval_valid), .score(eval_score)
  );

Line by line

  1. stand_pat is the condition for "captures only": depth 0, not in check, and not in perft mode (perft must count every move).
  2. The move generator writes into the move RAM; the search reads it at {ply, f.index}, so each ply has its own 256-entry region.
  3. The stack RAM is written at row ply when a legal move is entered (stack_we is high in S_LEGAL for a legal move), and read at row ply - 1, the parent, which is what a return needs.
  4. The evaluator reads pos directly; the search only pulses eval_start and waits for eval_valid.

The one attack tester, and the arithmetic for updating a node after a child returns. These are wires, computed continuously; the state machine just uses them in the right state.

Add to rtl/search_core.svpart 4 of 8
  // ---- the one attack test: uses "child", which also equals pos in S_ENTER -----
  logic attacker_side;
  bb_t  test_squares;
  always_comb begin
    if (state == S_TEST) begin           // did the mover leave its king attacked?
      attacker_side = child.side;
      test_squares  = safe_squares(child, move_r);
    end else begin                       // S_ENTER: is the side to move in check?
      attacker_side = ~child.side;
      test_squares  = child.bb[(child.side ? 6 : 0) + KING];
    end
  end
  always_ff @(posedge clk)
    attacked <= (side_attacks(child, attacker_side) & test_squares) != 64'b0;

  // ---- score arithmetic for S_SCORE ------------------------------------------
  logic signed [15:0] child_score, new_best, new_alpha;
  assign child_score = -ret;
  assign new_best    = (child_score > f.best)  ? child_score : f.best;
  assign new_alpha   = (child_score > f.alpha) ? child_score : f.alpha;

Line by line

  1. There is only one copy of the large attack logic (side_attacks), and it always looks at child. Two states share it by choosing what to test.
  2. In S_TEST the question is "after this move, is the mover's king attacked?": the attacker is the side now to move in child, and the squares are from safe_squares.
  3. In S_ENTER, child equals the new node's position (it was just copied into pos), so the same logic answers "is the side to move in check?".
  4. The answer is registered into attacked, so the long attack path has a whole clock. That is why S_TEST exists: one clock to compute, then S_LEGAL reads the result.
  5. child_score, new_best and new_alpha are the comparisons S_SCORE needs, computed as wires so S_SCORE can update everything in one clock.

31The search core: the state machine

Goal: the C negamax, one state per clock, matching the C exactly in nodes, score and best move.

Concept

Each state does one small piece of the C function:

StateThe C it matchesWhat it does
S_IDLEthe call from search()wait for start; load the root
S_ENTERnodes++count the node; the check test latches
S_CLASSIFYcheck, quiesce, the node limitstop on abort or limit; choose evaluate or generate
S_EVAL_WAITstand patwait for valid; return on a cutoff, otherwise raise alpha
S_GEN_START, S_GEN_WAITgenerate_movesstart the generator and wait for done
S_NEXTthe for testend of list? Otherwise the RAM is reading this move
S_READlist[i]store the move
S_DECODE, S_APPLYmake_movebuild child, in two clocks
S_TESTlegal_afterthe attack test latches
S_LEGALcontinue, or the recursive callillegal: next move. Legal: push, and enter the child
S_END_NODEthe mate and stalemate testreturn mate, stalemate, or best
S_RETURNreturnat ply 0, finish; otherwise the stack RAM is reading the parent
S_POPthe call returningrestore pos, f, ply
S_SCOREscore = -..., the updates, breakupdate best and alpha; cut off or go to the next move

Abort and the node limit are both checked in one place, S_CLASSIFY. The core can simply stop there, without unwinding the stack, because a stopped search's position and frames are thrown away. The CPU ignores the aborted result and keeps the answer from its last finished search.

Code

Entering a node: count it, classify it, evaluate if it is a leaf, and generate its moves.

Add to rtl/search_core.svpart 5 of 8
  // ---- the state machine -----------------------------------------------------
  always_ff @(posedge clk) begin
    done       <= 1'b0;
    gen_start  <= 1'b0;
    eval_start <= 1'b0;
    if (busy) cycles <= cycles + 48'd1;
    if (abort && busy) abort_pending <= 1'b1;

    if (rst) begin
      state <= S_IDLE;
      busy <= 1'b0;
      aborted <= 1'b0;
      fault <= 1'b0;
      abort_pending <= 1'b0;
      nodes <= 48'd0;
      cycles <= 48'd0;
      best_move <= '0;
      best_score <= '0;
    end else begin
      case (state)
        S_IDLE: if (start) begin
          pos <= root;
          child <= root;
          f <= '{alpha: -SCORE_INF, beta: SCORE_INF, best: -SCORE_INF,
                 depth: depth, index: 8'd0, count: 8'd0,
                 any_legal: 1'b0, in_check: 1'b0};
          ply <= 5'd0;
          nodes <= 48'd0;
          cycles <= 48'd0;
          best_move <= '0;
          best_score <= '0;
          aborted <= 1'b0;
          fault <= 1'b0;
          abort_pending <= 1'b0;
          limit_on <= (node_limit != 32'd0);
          busy <= 1'b1;
          state <= S_ENTER;
        end

Line by line: the defaults and S_IDLE

  1. The first lines run on every clock. done, gen_start and eval_start default to 0, so whenever a state sets one of them it becomes a one-clock pulse.
  2. cycles counts every clock while busy. An ABORT that arrives at any time is remembered in abort_pending and acted on at the next node.
  3. S_IDLE: on start, copy the root into both pos and child (the attack tester looks at child), set up the root frame with the full window (-INF, +INF), clear the counters, and remember whether a node limit is in force.

Every node then starts the same way:

Add to rtl/search_core.svpart 6 of 8
        // A node begins here. "attacked" latches the check test at this edge.
        S_ENTER: begin
          if (!perft_mode || f.depth == 5'd0) nodes <= nodes + 48'd1;
          state <= S_CLASSIFY;
        end

        S_CLASSIFY: begin
          f.in_check <= attacked;
          if (abort_pending || (limit_on && nodes == 48'(node_limit))) begin
            aborted <= 1'b1;           // stop at once: the CPU ignores this result
            busy <= 1'b0;
            done <= 1'b1;
            state <= S_IDLE;
          end else if (perft_mode) begin
            ret <= 16'sd0;
            state <= (f.depth == 5'd0) ? S_RETURN : S_GEN_START;
          end else if (ply == 5'(MAX_PLY - 1) || (f.depth == 5'd0 && !attacked)) begin
            eval_start <= 1'b1;
            state <= S_EVAL_WAIT;
          end else begin
            state <= S_GEN_START;
          end
        end

        S_EVAL_WAIT: if (eval_valid) begin
          if (ply == 5'(MAX_PLY - 1) || eval_score >= f.beta) begin
            ret <= eval_score;
            state <= S_RETURN;
          end else begin
            f.best <= eval_score;
            if (eval_score > f.alpha) f.alpha <= eval_score;
            state <= S_GEN_START;
          end
        end

        S_GEN_START: begin
          gen_start <= 1'b1;
          state <= S_GEN_WAIT;
        end

        S_GEN_WAIT: if (gen_done) begin
          if (gen_overflow) fault <= 1'b1;
          f.count <= gen_count;
          f.index <= 8'd0;
          state <= S_NEXT;
        end

Line by line: entering a node

  1. S_ENTER counts the node (in perft mode, only leaves are counted). During this clock the attack tester is already checking whether the side to move is in check, because child holds this node's position.
  2. S_CLASSIFY stores that answer in f.in_check and makes the big decision. Abort or node limit: stop at once and report ABORTED. Perft: count the leaf or generate. Search: at depth 0 and not in check, or at the deepest ply, this is a stand-pat node, so start the evaluator; otherwise generate moves.
  3. S_EVAL_WAIT waits for eval_valid. At the deepest ply, return the static score whatever it is. If it is already at least beta, return it too: the opponent will avoid this position anyway. Otherwise it becomes best, may raise alpha, and the node goes on to try its captures.
  4. S_GEN_START / S_GEN_WAIT: pulse the generator and wait for done. Then this node's list sits in the move RAM at {ply, 0} onward; store its length in f.count and start at index 0.

Trying moves: read, decode, apply, test, and either skip an illegal move or push and enter the child. Notice the new frame's window in S_LEGAL: alpha: -f.beta, beta: -f.alpha, exactly the C call's -beta, -alpha.

Add to rtl/search_core.svpart 7 of 8
        // The RAM address {ply, f.index} is sampled at this clock edge.
        S_NEXT: begin
          if (f.index == f.count) state <= S_END_NODE;
          else                    state <= S_READ;
        end

        S_READ: begin
          move_r <= move_rdata;
          if (ply == 5'd0) root_move <= move_rdata;
          state <= S_DECODE;
        end

        S_DECODE: begin
          decoded <= decode_move(pos, move_r);
          state <= S_APPLY;
        end

        S_APPLY: begin
          child <= apply_decoded(pos, decoded);
          state <= S_TEST;
        end

        S_TEST: state <= S_LEGAL;      // "attacked" latches at this edge

        S_LEGAL: begin
          if (attacked) begin          // illegal move: try the next one
            f.index <= f.index + 8'd1;
            state <= S_NEXT;
          end else begin               // legal: stack_we pushes {pos, f} at this edge
            pos <= child;
            f <= '{alpha: -f.beta, beta: -f.alpha, best: -SCORE_INF,
                   depth: (f.depth == 5'd0) ? 5'd0 : f.depth - 5'd1,
                   index: 8'd0, count: 8'd0, any_legal: 1'b0, in_check: 1'b0};
            ply <= ply + 5'd1;
            state <= S_ENTER;
          end
        end

Line by line: trying one move

  1. S_NEXT is the for test. If every move has been tried, finish the node. Otherwise the RAM is reading address {ply, f.index} during this clock.
  2. S_READ stores the move. At the root it is also saved in root_move, because if this move turns out best, that is what the CPU will receive.
  3. S_DECODE and S_APPLY are the two clocks of make_move from Step 26, producing child.
  4. S_TEST waits one clock while the attack tester checks child: is the mover's king (or a castling square) attacked?
  5. S_LEGAL: if attacked, the move is illegal, so skip it. If legal, this is the recursive call: stack_we writes {pos, f} into row ply of the stack RAM at this very edge, while pos becomes child, the frame is set up for the child with the window negated and swapped, and ply goes up by one.

Returning: finish the node, pop the parent, and update it with the child's score. child_score = -ret is the negamax minus sign.

Add to rtl/search_core.svpart 8 of 8
        S_END_NODE: begin
          if (!f.any_legal && !stand_pat)
            ret <= f.in_check ? (-SCORE_MATE + 16'(ply)) : 16'sd0;
          else
            ret <= f.best;
          state <= S_RETURN;
        end

        S_RETURN: begin
          if (ply == 5'd0) begin
            best_score <= ret;
            busy <= 1'b0;
            done <= 1'b1;
            state <= S_IDLE;
          end else begin
            state <= S_POP;            // the stack address is sampled at this edge
          end
        end

        S_POP: begin
          pos <= stack_rdata.pos;
          f <= stack_rdata.f;
          ply <= ply - 5'd1;
          state <= S_SCORE;
        end

        S_SCORE: begin
          f.any_legal <= 1'b1;         // we only came back because a move was legal
          f.best <= new_best;
          f.alpha <= new_alpha;
          if (child_score > f.best && ply == 5'd0) best_move <= root_move;
          if (!perft_mode && new_alpha >= f.beta) begin
            ret <= new_best;           // beta cutoff
            state <= S_RETURN;
          end else begin
            f.index <= f.index + 8'd1;
            state <= S_NEXT;
          end
        end

        default: state <= S_IDLE;
      endcase
    end
  end
endmodule

Line by line: returning

  1. S_END_NODE: no legal move at all means checkmate (score -MATE + ply, so a quicker mate scores higher for the winner) or stalemate (0). Otherwise return best.
  2. S_RETURN: at the root, publish the score and finish. Anywhere else, the stack RAM is reading row ply - 1, the parent.
  3. S_POP restores the parent's position and frame and decreases ply. This is the moment the C call returns.
  4. S_SCORE is the code after the recursive call: negate the child's score (child_score = -ret), update best and alpha, record the root move if it is a new best, and either cut off (alpha >= beta: return at once) or move on to the next index.

Where the clocks go

An interior node costs, roughly: 2 clocks to enter and classify, about 55 for the generator to write its list (Step 29), then for each move 6 clocks to read, decode, apply, test and push, and 3 to pop and score when the child returns. A leaf in quiescence is cheaper: enter, classify, a few clocks for the evaluation pipeline, then return at once if it stands pat. Averaged over a real search, that is the 45 to 50 clocks per node the testbench reports, about a million nodes a second at 50 MHz.

Two design choices keep that number low. First, the stack RAM is read only on a return, and written only on a call, so neither ever waits for the other. Second, an illegal move costs only its own 6 clocks: the attack test on child rejects it before anything is pushed, exactly like legal_after in the C.

Check

This is the big one. For every test, the hardware must visit the same number of nodes as the C, and reach the same score and the same best move.

Create tb/tb_search.sv
// tb_search.sv - complete searches and perfts: nodes, score and best move must
// all match the C engine exactly.
`timescale 1ns / 1ps
module tb_search;
  import chess_pkg::*;

  logic clk = 1'b0;
  logic rst = 1'b1;
  logic start = 1'b0;
  logic abort = 1'b0;
  position_t root, next_root;
  logic [4:0] depth;
  logic perft_mode;
  logic [31:0] node_limit;
  logic busy, done, aborted, fault;
  move_t best_move;
  logic signed [15:0] best_score;
  logic [47:0] nodes, cycles;
  always #5 clk = ~clk;

  search_core dut (.clk, .rst, .start, .abort, .root, .depth, .perft_mode, .node_limit,
                   .busy, .done, .aborted, .fault, .best_move, .best_score, .nodes, .cycles);

  initial begin
    int fd, errors, checked, r, side, castle, ep, mode, d, score_x, abort_x;
    longint limit_x, nodes_x;
    longint total_nodes, total_cycles;
    logic [63:0] b;
    logic [15:0] best_x;
    errors = 0;
    checked = 0;
    total_nodes = 0;
    total_cycles = 0;
    repeat (3) @(negedge clk);
    rst = 1'b0;
    fd = $fopen("vec_search.txt", "r");
    if (fd == 0) $fatal(1, "cannot open vec_search.txt");
    while (!$feof(fd)) begin
      for (int i = 0; i < 12; i++) begin
        r = $fscanf(fd, "%h", b);
        next_root.bb[i] = b;
      end
      r = $fscanf(fd, "%d %d %d %d %d %d %d %d %h %d\n",
                  side, castle, ep, mode, d, limit_x, nodes_x, score_x, best_x, abort_x);
      if (r != 10) break;
      next_root.side = side[0];
      next_root.castle = castle[3:0];
      next_root.ep = ep[6:0];
      @(negedge clk);
      root = next_root;
      depth = d[4:0];
      perft_mode = (mode == 1);
      node_limit = limit_x[31:0];
      start = 1'b1;
      @(negedge clk);
      start = 1'b0;
      while (done !== 1'b1) @(negedge clk);
      checked++;
      if (mode == 0 && abort_x == 0) begin
        total_nodes += nodes;
        total_cycles += cycles;
      end
      if (longint'(nodes) != nodes_x || int'(aborted) != abort_x || fault) begin
        errors++;
        $display("NODE MISMATCH: test %0d mode %0d depth %0d got %0d expected %0d aborted %b",
                 checked, mode, d, nodes, nodes_x, aborted);
      end
      if (mode == 0 && abort_x == 0
          && (int'(best_score) != score_x || {1'b0, best_move} !== best_x)) begin
        errors++;
        $display("RESULT MISMATCH: test %0d depth %0d got %0d %h expected %0d %h",
                 checked, d, best_score, best_move, score_x, best_x);
      end
    end
    $display("checked %0d searches, errors = %0d", checked, errors);
    $display("alpha-beta average: %0d.%0d clocks per node",
             total_cycles / total_nodes, (10 * total_cycles / total_nodes) % 10);
    if (errors == 0) $display("TB_SEARCH PASS");
    else             $display("TB_SEARCH FAIL");
    $finish;
  end
endmodule
Command Prompt
scripts\run_sim.bat tb_search
Expected output
checked 167 searches, errors = 0
alpha-beta average: 44.1 clocks per node
TB_SEARCH PASS

An off-by-one anywhere in the search changes a node count almost at once, so this one line means a lot. If it fails, find the first failing test and work down this list:

  1. Perft mismatches first. They mean the rules or the stack are wrong; search results mean nothing until they are fixed.
  2. Perft passes, but alpha-beta node counts differ. Suspect the window (negate and swap) or a comparison done as unsigned. In the waveform, show alpha, beta and ret as signed decimal.
  3. Nodes match, the score differs. Suspect S_END_NODE, or stand pat in S_EVAL_WAIT.
  4. The score matches, the move differs. Suspect root_move or the ply == 0 test.

To see waveforms, add -debug typical to the xelab line in run_sim.bat, then run xsim tb_search_sim -gui from the sim folder.

32The AXI4-Lite register block

Goal: let the Cortex-A9 load a position, start a search and read the result, then test the whole design over the bus.

Concept

The Cortex-A9 talks to the programmable logic over AXI4-Lite, a simple bus for reading and writing 32-bit registers. To the C program, each register is just a memory address. A write uses three channels: the address, the data, and a response. A read uses two: the address and the data. Each channel has a valid signal (the sender has something) and a ready signal (the receiver can take it). A transfer happens on a clock edge where both are high.

Register map

All registers are 32 bits wide; always use full 32-bit accesses.

OffsetNameAccessMeaning
0x00IDreadalways 0xC4E55A01: the first thing to check
0x04CONTROLwritebit 0 START, bit 1 ABORT
0x08STATUSreadbit 0 BUSY, bit 1 DONE, bit 2 ABORTED, bit 3 FAULT
0x0CDEPTHread/writesearch depth, 0 to 31
0x10MODEread/write0 search, 1 perft
0x14NODE_LIMITread/write0 means no limit
0x18METAread/writebit 0 side to move, bits 4:1 castling rights, bits 11:5 en-passant square
0x1CBEST_MOVEreadmove word; 0 means no legal move
0x20SCOREreadsigned, from the side to move's view
0x24, 0x28NODESreadlow and high words; leaves in perft mode
0x2C, 0x30CYCLESreadclocks used by the last search
0x40 to 0x9CBOARDSwrite24 words: board 0 low, board 0 high, board 1 low, ...

Why a shadow copy? The CPU writes the 26 position registers one at a time. If the search used them directly, it could see a half-written board. Instead they fill a shadow copy, and START copies all 780 bits into the core in one clock. Writes are ignored while the core is busy, so a running search can never be disturbed.

Code

The module has five groups of ports, one per AXI channel, plus the clock and reset. The names follow Xilinx's convention (s_axi_ for a slave, then the channel and signal), which is what lets Vivado recognise the whole group as one bus later.

Create rtl/chess_axi.svpart 1 of 6
// chess_axi.sv - AXI4-Lite register block around search_core.
// The CPU writes a shadow copy of the position; START copies it into the core
// in one clock, so the search can never see a half-written board.
`timescale 1ns / 1ps
module chess_axi
  import chess_pkg::*;
(
    input  logic        aclk,
    input  logic        aresetn,
    // write address
    input  logic [11:0] s_axi_awaddr,
    input  logic        s_axi_awvalid,
    output logic        s_axi_awready,
    // write data
    input  logic [31:0] s_axi_wdata,
    input  logic [3:0]  s_axi_wstrb,
    input  logic        s_axi_wvalid,
    output logic        s_axi_wready,
    // write response
    output logic [1:0]  s_axi_bresp,
    output logic        s_axi_bvalid,
    input  logic        s_axi_bready,
    // read address
    input  logic [11:0] s_axi_araddr,
    input  logic        s_axi_arvalid,
    output logic        s_axi_arready,
    // read data
    output logic [31:0] s_axi_rdata,
    output logic [1:0]  s_axi_rresp,
    output logic        s_axi_rvalid,
    input  logic        s_axi_rready
);
  localparam logic [31:0] CHESS_ID = 32'hC4E5_5A01;

  // Word offsets. Byte address = word offset * 4.
  localparam logic [9:0] R_ID = 10'd0, R_CONTROL = 10'd1, R_STATUS = 10'd2,
                         R_DEPTH = 10'd3, R_MODE = 10'd4, R_NODE_LIMIT = 10'd5,
                         R_META = 10'd6, R_BEST_MOVE = 10'd7, R_SCORE = 10'd8,
                         R_NODES_LO = 10'd9, R_NODES_HI = 10'd10,
                         R_CYCLES_LO = 10'd11, R_CYCLES_HI = 10'd12,
                         R_BOARD_FIRST = 10'd16;   // 24 words: board 0 low, board 0 high, ...

Line by line

  1. Write address channel (awaddr, awvalid, awready): the CPU puts the byte address it wants to write on awaddr and raises awvalid. Twelve address bits are enough because the block occupies a 4 KB window; the interconnect strips off the upper bits (0x43C0_0000) before they reach us.
  2. Write data channel (wdata, wstrb, wvalid, wready): the 32-bit value. wstrb says which of the four bytes are valid; we ask the CPU to always write whole words, so we ignore it.
  3. Write response channel (bresp, bvalid, bready): after taking a write we answer "OKAY" (bresp = 00). The CPU's store instruction is not complete until it sees this.
  4. Read address (ar...) and read data (r...) channels: the same idea for loads. The answer comes back on rdata with rvalid.
  5. Word offsets. Registers are 4 bytes apart, so byte address 0x08 is word 2. The code compares word numbers (awaddr[11:2]) because they are smaller and match the table above directly: R_STATUS = 2 is byte offset 0x08. The board words start at word 16, byte 0x40.

Next, the storage behind the registers. The CPU never writes into the search core directly; it writes into these flip-flops, and the core reads them only at the moment it starts.

Add to rtl/chess_axi.svpart 2 of 6
  // ---- shadow registers ------------------------------------------------------
  logic [23:0][31:0] board_regs;
  logic [31:0] meta_reg, limit_reg;
  logic [4:0]  depth_reg;
  logic        mode_reg;

  // ---- core ------------------------------------------------------------------
  logic        core_start, core_abort, core_busy, core_done, core_aborted, core_fault;
  logic        done_sticky;
  position_t   root_pos;
  move_t       core_best;
  logic signed [15:0] core_score;
  logic [47:0] core_nodes, core_cycles;

  always_comb begin
    for (int i = 0; i < 12; i++)
      root_pos.bb[i] = {board_regs[2*i + 1], board_regs[2*i]};
    root_pos.side   = meta_reg[0];
    root_pos.castle = meta_reg[4:1];
    root_pos.ep     = meta_reg[11:5];
  end

  search_core u_core (
    .clk(aclk), .rst(!aresetn), .start(core_start), .abort(core_abort),
    .root(root_pos), .depth(depth_reg), .perft_mode(mode_reg), .node_limit(limit_reg),
    .busy(core_busy), .done(core_done), .aborted(core_aborted), .fault(core_fault),
    .best_move(core_best), .best_score(core_score),
    .nodes(core_nodes), .cycles(core_cycles)
  );

Line by line

  1. board_regs is 24 registers of 32 bits: two per bitboard, because a bitboard is 64 bits and an AXI4-Lite word is 32. Word 2i holds the low half of board i, word 2i+1 the high half.
  2. meta_reg packs the three small fields: side to move in bit 0, castling rights in bits 4 to 1, en-passant square in bits 11 to 5. depth_reg, mode_reg and limit_reg are the search settings.
  3. The always_comb block is pure wiring. It glues each pair of words back into a 64-bit board, {high, low}, and slices the META fields out, building a complete position_t called root_pos. No logic, no clock: just a different view of the same flip-flops.
  4. The core's root input is connected to root_pos. In S_IDLE, on the clock where start is high, the core copies root into its own pos register (Step 31). That copy is the "snapshot": all 780 bits at once.

The write channel, in two parts. First the handshake, which decides when a write happens:

Add to rtl/chess_axi.svpart 3 of 6
  // ---- write channel: accept AW and W together, answer with B ------------------
  logic       write_fire;
  logic [9:0] waddr_word;
  assign s_axi_awready = s_axi_awvalid && s_axi_wvalid && !s_axi_bvalid;
  assign s_axi_wready  = s_axi_awready;
  assign s_axi_bresp   = 2'b00;
  assign write_fire    = s_axi_awready;           // both channels valid this clock
  assign waddr_word    = s_axi_awaddr[11:2];

  assign core_start = write_fire && waddr_word == R_CONTROL && s_axi_wdata[0] && !core_busy;
  assign core_abort = write_fire && waddr_word == R_CONTROL && s_axi_wdata[1];

Line by line

  1. awready is high only when the address and the data are both being offered, and we are not still waiting to deliver the previous response. AXI allows the two to arrive on different clocks; by waiting for both we never need to store one while waiting for the other. This is the simplest correct AXI4-Lite slave.
  2. wready equals awready, so both channels complete on the same clock edge. That edge is called write_fire: "a write is happening now".
  3. core_start is a one-clock pulse: a write to CONTROL with bit 0 set, while the core is idle. core_abort is the same for bit 1, and works only while the core is busy (the core ignores it otherwise).

Then the registers, which decide what a write does:

Add to rtl/chess_axi.svpart 4 of 6
  always_ff @(posedge aclk) begin
    if (!aresetn) begin
      s_axi_bvalid <= 1'b0;
      done_sticky  <= 1'b0;
      depth_reg    <= 5'd1;
      mode_reg     <= 1'b0;
      limit_reg    <= 32'd0;
      meta_reg     <= 32'd0;
      board_regs   <= '0;
    end else begin
      if (s_axi_bvalid && s_axi_bready) s_axi_bvalid <= 1'b0;
      if (core_start) done_sticky <= 1'b0;
      if (core_done)  done_sticky <= 1'b1;
      if (write_fire) begin
        s_axi_bvalid <= 1'b1;
        // Registers may only change while the core is idle.
        if (!core_busy) begin
          case (waddr_word)
            R_DEPTH:      depth_reg <= s_axi_wdata[4:0];
            R_MODE:       mode_reg  <= s_axi_wdata[0];
            R_NODE_LIMIT: limit_reg <= s_axi_wdata;
            R_META:       meta_reg  <= s_axi_wdata;
            default:
              if (waddr_word >= R_BOARD_FIRST && waddr_word < R_BOARD_FIRST + 10'd24)
                board_regs[5'(waddr_word - R_BOARD_FIRST)] <= s_axi_wdata;
          endcase
        end
      end
    end
  end

Line by line

  1. On reset, everything is cleared and the depth is set to 1, a safe default.
  2. bvalid goes high one clock after a write fires, and drops once the CPU has taken the response (bvalid && bready). While it is high, awready stays low, so a second write waits its turn.
  3. done_sticky remembers that a search finished. The core's done is a one-clock pulse, far too short for a CPU to catch by polling, so this bit holds it until the next START clears it. STATUS bit 1 reads this register.
  4. The case stores the data in the register the address selects. The default branch handles the 24 board words with one range check: word 16 goes to board_regs[0], word 39 to board_regs[23].
  5. Everything is inside if (!core_busy): while a search runs, writes are acknowledged (the CPU must not hang) but have no effect. So nothing the CPU does can change a position under a running search.

The read channel, also in two parts. First, what each address reads as:

Add to rtl/chess_axi.svpart 5 of 6
  // ---- read channel ------------------------------------------------------------
  logic [9:0]  raddr_word;
  logic [31:0] read_value;
  assign raddr_word    = s_axi_araddr[11:2];
  assign s_axi_arready = s_axi_arvalid && !s_axi_rvalid;
  assign s_axi_rresp   = 2'b00;

  always_comb begin
    case (raddr_word)
      R_ID:         read_value = CHESS_ID;
      R_STATUS:     read_value = {28'd0, core_fault, core_aborted, done_sticky, core_busy};
      R_DEPTH:      read_value = {27'd0, depth_reg};
      R_MODE:       read_value = {31'd0, mode_reg};
      R_NODE_LIMIT: read_value = limit_reg;
      R_META:       read_value = meta_reg;
      R_BEST_MOVE:  read_value = {17'd0, core_best};
      R_SCORE:      read_value = 32'(core_score);
      R_NODES_LO:   read_value = core_nodes[31:0];
      R_NODES_HI:   read_value = {16'd0, core_nodes[47:32]};
      R_CYCLES_LO:  read_value = core_cycles[31:0];
      R_CYCLES_HI:  read_value = {16'd0, core_cycles[47:32]};
      default:      read_value = 32'd0;
    endcase
  end

Line by line

  1. arready accepts a read address whenever we are not still holding a previous answer.
  2. The always_comb case is a multiplexer: for each word address, which value would be returned. STATUS packs four bits: BUSY, DONE (the sticky copy), ABORTED, FAULT.
  3. 32'(core_score) sign-extends the 16-bit score, so a negative score reads as a negative 32-bit number and C can simply cast it to int32_t.
  4. Node and clock counters are 48 bits wide, so they need two words each. The board registers are write-only: reading them returns 0, which saves 24 inputs on this multiplexer.

Then the reply, registered so the data leaves on a clean clock edge:

Add to rtl/chess_axi.svpart 6 of 6
  always_ff @(posedge aclk) begin
    if (!aresetn) begin
      s_axi_rvalid <= 1'b0;
      s_axi_rdata  <= 32'd0;
    end else begin
      if (s_axi_rvalid && s_axi_rready) s_axi_rvalid <= 1'b0;
      if (s_axi_arready) begin
        s_axi_rvalid <= 1'b1;
        s_axi_rdata  <= read_value;
      end
    end
  end
endmodule

Line by line

  1. When a read address is accepted, the looked-up value is stored in rdata and rvalid rises on the next clock.
  2. rvalid stays high until the CPU takes the data (rready). A read therefore costs two clocks inside this block; most of the time a CPU read spends is in the interconnect and the processor, not here.

One more file. Vivado's block design can't use a SystemVerilog module as the top of a "module reference" (UG994 lists this limit). So this plain Verilog file wraps it.

Create rtl/chess_axi_top.v
// chess_axi_top.v - Vivado's "Add Module" needs a plain Verilog top level, because
// a block-design module reference cannot have a SystemVerilog top. This file only
// renames ports and adds the interface hints.
`timescale 1ns / 1ps
module chess_axi_top (
    (* X_INTERFACE_INFO = "xilinx.com:signal:clock:1.0 aclk CLK" *)
    (* X_INTERFACE_PARAMETER = "ASSOCIATED_BUSIF s_axi, ASSOCIATED_RESET aresetn" *)
    input  wire        aclk,
    (* X_INTERFACE_INFO = "xilinx.com:signal:reset:1.0 aresetn RST" *)
    (* X_INTERFACE_PARAMETER = "POLARITY ACTIVE_LOW" *)
    input  wire        aresetn,
    input  wire [11:0] s_axi_awaddr,
    input  wire [2:0]  s_axi_awprot,
    input  wire        s_axi_awvalid,
    output wire        s_axi_awready,
    input  wire [31:0] s_axi_wdata,
    input  wire [3:0]  s_axi_wstrb,
    input  wire        s_axi_wvalid,
    output wire        s_axi_wready,
    output wire [1:0]  s_axi_bresp,
    output wire        s_axi_bvalid,
    input  wire        s_axi_bready,
    input  wire [11:0] s_axi_araddr,
    input  wire [2:0]  s_axi_arprot,
    input  wire        s_axi_arvalid,
    output wire        s_axi_arready,
    output wire [31:0] s_axi_rdata,
    output wire [1:0]  s_axi_rresp,
    output wire        s_axi_rvalid,
    input  wire        s_axi_rready
);
  chess_axi u_chess_axi (
    .aclk(aclk), .aresetn(aresetn),
    .s_axi_awaddr(s_axi_awaddr), .s_axi_awvalid(s_axi_awvalid), .s_axi_awready(s_axi_awready),
    .s_axi_wdata(s_axi_wdata), .s_axi_wstrb(s_axi_wstrb),
    .s_axi_wvalid(s_axi_wvalid), .s_axi_wready(s_axi_wready),
    .s_axi_bresp(s_axi_bresp), .s_axi_bvalid(s_axi_bvalid), .s_axi_bready(s_axi_bready),
    .s_axi_araddr(s_axi_araddr), .s_axi_arvalid(s_axi_arvalid), .s_axi_arready(s_axi_arready),
    .s_axi_rdata(s_axi_rdata), .s_axi_rresp(s_axi_rresp),
    .s_axi_rvalid(s_axi_rvalid), .s_axi_rready(s_axi_rready)
  );
endmodule

Line by line

  1. X_INTERFACE_INFO ... clock on aclk tells Vivado "this pin is a clock". ASSOCIATED_BUSIF s_axi says the s_axi bus is synchronous to it, so Connection Automation will connect the same clock that drives the bus master. ASSOCIATED_RESET aresetn pairs the reset with it.
  2. POLARITY ACTIVE_LOW on aresetn: the core is in reset while this pin is 0, which is what the Processor System Reset block produces.
  3. The bus pins need no attributes: because every name starts with s_axi_ and ends in a standard AXI signal name, Vivado infers an AXI4-Lite slave interface called s_axi by itself.
  4. awprot and arprot (protection type) exist only so the interface is complete; the core does not use them.
Check

This testbench plays the part of the Cortex-A9: every action goes over AXI, with the address and data deliberately offered on different clocks. It runs 40 searches from the vector file, then starts a long perft and aborts it.

Create tb/tb_axi.sv
// tb_axi.sv - plays the part of the Cortex-A9: every access goes over AXI4-Lite.
`timescale 1ns / 1ps
module tb_axi;
  parameter int MAX_TESTS = 40;
  logic aclk = 1'b0;
  logic aresetn = 1'b0;
  logic [11:0] awaddr, araddr;
  logic awvalid = 1'b0, wvalid = 1'b0, bready = 1'b0, arvalid = 1'b0, rready = 1'b0;
  logic awready, wready, bvalid, arready, rvalid;
  logic [31:0] wdata, rdata;
  logic [1:0] bresp, rresp;
  always #5 aclk = ~aclk;

  chess_axi_top dut (
    .aclk, .aresetn,
    .s_axi_awaddr(awaddr), .s_axi_awprot(3'b000), .s_axi_awvalid(awvalid), .s_axi_awready(awready),
    .s_axi_wdata(wdata), .s_axi_wstrb(4'hF), .s_axi_wvalid(wvalid), .s_axi_wready(wready),
    .s_axi_bresp(bresp), .s_axi_bvalid(bvalid), .s_axi_bready(bready),
    .s_axi_araddr(araddr), .s_axi_arprot(3'b000), .s_axi_arvalid(arvalid), .s_axi_arready(arready),
    .s_axi_rdata(rdata), .s_axi_rresp(rresp), .s_axi_rvalid(rvalid), .s_axi_rready(rready)
  );

  // Address and data are offered on separate clocks on purpose, to prove the
  // slave waits for both.
  task automatic axi_write(input logic [11:0] addr, input logic [31:0] data);
    @(negedge aclk);
    awaddr = addr;
    awvalid = 1'b1;
    @(negedge aclk);
    wdata = data;
    wvalid = 1'b1;
    bready = 1'b1;
    while (awready !== 1'b1) @(negedge aclk);
    @(negedge aclk);               // the handshake happened at the rising edge
    awvalid = 1'b0;
    wvalid = 1'b0;
    while (bvalid !== 1'b1) @(negedge aclk);
    @(negedge aclk);
    bready = 1'b0;
  endtask

  task automatic axi_read(input logic [11:0] addr, output logic [31:0] data);
    @(negedge aclk);
    araddr = addr;
    arvalid = 1'b1;
    rready = 1'b1;
    while (arready !== 1'b1) @(negedge aclk);
    @(negedge aclk);
    arvalid = 1'b0;
    while (rvalid !== 1'b1) @(negedge aclk);
    data = rdata;
    @(negedge aclk);
    rready = 1'b0;
  endtask

  initial begin
    int fd, errors, checked, r, side, castle, ep, mode, d, score_x, abort_x;
    longint limit_x, nodes_x;
    logic [63:0] b;
    logic [15:0] best_x;
    logic [31:0] v, nodes_lo, nodes_hi, best, score;
    errors = 0;
    checked = 0;
    repeat (5) @(negedge aclk);
    aresetn = 1'b1;

    axi_read(12'h000, v);
    if (v !== 32'hC4E55A01) begin
      errors++;
      $display("BAD ID %h", v);
    end

    fd = $fopen("vec_search.txt", "r");
    if (fd == 0) $fatal(1, "cannot open vec_search.txt");
    while (!$feof(fd) && checked < MAX_TESTS) begin
      for (int i = 0; i < 12; i++) begin
        r = $fscanf(fd, "%h", b);
        axi_write(12'h040 + 12'(8*i),     b[31:0]);
        axi_write(12'h040 + 12'(8*i) + 4, b[63:32]);
      end
      r = $fscanf(fd, "%d %d %d %d %d %d %d %d %h %d\n",
                  side, castle, ep, mode, d, limit_x, nodes_x, score_x, best_x, abort_x);
      if (r != 10) break;
      axi_write(12'h018, side | (castle << 1) | (ep << 5));
      axi_write(12'h00C, d);
      axi_write(12'h010, mode);
      axi_write(12'h014, limit_x[31:0]);
      axi_write(12'h004, 32'd1);                  // START
      do axi_read(12'h008, v); while (v[1] !== 1'b1);   // wait for DONE
      axi_read(12'h01C, best);
      axi_read(12'h020, score);
      axi_read(12'h024, nodes_lo);
      axi_read(12'h028, nodes_hi);
      checked++;
      if (longint'({nodes_hi, nodes_lo}) != nodes_x || int'(v[2]) != abort_x) begin
        errors++;
        $display("NODES: test %0d got %0d expected %0d", checked, nodes_lo, nodes_x);
      end
      if (mode == 0 && abort_x == 0
          && (int'($signed(score)) != score_x || best[15:0] !== best_x)) begin
        errors++;
        $display("RESULT: test %0d got %0d %h expected %0d %h",
                 checked, $signed(score), best, score_x, best_x);
      end
    end

    // A running search must obey ABORT.
    axi_write(12'h00C, 32'd8);
    axi_write(12'h010, 32'd1);
    axi_write(12'h014, 32'd0);
    axi_write(12'h004, 32'd1);
    axi_read(12'h008, v);
    if (v[0] !== 1'b1) begin errors++; $display("core did not go busy"); end
    axi_write(12'h004, 32'd2);
    do axi_read(12'h008, v); while (v[1] !== 1'b1);
    if (v[2] !== 1'b1) begin errors++; $display("abort flag not set"); end

    $display("checked %0d searches over AXI, errors = %0d", checked, errors);
    if (errors == 0) $display("TB_AXI PASS");
    else             $display("TB_AXI FAIL");
    $finish;
  end
endmodule
Command Prompt
scripts\run_sim.bat tb_axi
Expected output
checked 40 searches over AXI, errors = 0
TB_AXI PASS
